Before

On The 1 st Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 467 of 2013
 Motilal
 Versus
 Ramesh Chandra And 2 Ors.

And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri J.M. Poonegar - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Saranjit Singh Chawla, learned counsel for the r  ORDER

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant against the award dated 3.10.2012 passed in MACC.No.268/2011 whereby the appellant/injured Motilal has been awarded an amount of Rs.3,00,889/- on account of injuries received to him in the accident occurred on 16.6.2012.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant has pressed the appeal only on the point of contributory negligence.

His submission is that injured was travelling on moped along with his wife and he was hit by the offending car bearing registration No.M.P. 09 CB 1351, which was driven by the respondent No.1 rashly and negligently.

There was no negligence on the part of the injured and ignoring the evidence learned claims tribunal has taken contributory negligence equal to 50% on the part of the injured which is not proper as per the evidence therefore, the contributory negligence on the part NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8572 2 MA-467-2013 of the claimant /
appellant should be set aside.
It is also submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle has not been examined.
Beside this no other point has been raised by the appellant and prays that the appeal be allowed.

Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Co. has opposed the prayer and submitted that the claimant and driver of the offending vehicle/car were equally liable for the accident and therefore, claims tribunal has not committed any error in saddling the liability of 50% contributory negligence even on the part of the appellant hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: From the evidence available on record, it is apparent that claimant was driving on moped and while he was taking turn on the spot, the accident took place with the driver of the car.

The learned claims tribunal has examined the evidence with regard to the contributory negligence in para 15 and 16 of the impugned award, but looking to the evidence available on record, the claimant cannot be held liable for more than 20% contributory negligence as he was driving the moped and it was the liability of the driver of the car to larger extent to avoid the accident.
Thus the percentage of contributory negligence on the part of the claimant is reduced from 50% to 20%.

Thus after deducting 20% from the total amount awarded Rs.3,00,889/- the appellant is entitled to receive Rs.2,40,711/- (Rs.3,00,889 - 20%) as compensation with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal.
Hence 20% amount ie., Rs.60,177/- will be deducted from NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8572 3 MA-467-2013 the awarded compensation of Rs.3,00,889/- by the claims tribunal.
Court fees, if any, is required to be deposited, then the same shall paid within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order on the enhanced amount.

It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the appellant will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount beyond 30 days' period,
till the payment of requisite court fees.
Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed off.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
